term: accessibility and components in the Hume tests
definition: Reuse Modal.Frame and the Scott embedding’s MProp, Box and Dia only. The conditional propagation laws assume symmetry and transitivity; therefore apply to S5 equivalence frames, although reflexivity is unnecessary. Their scope is the accessible component, not all worlds. Universal Bool is equivalence accessibility; branching Bool is reflexive/transitive but not symmetric. Identity-accessibility Bool has two isolated components. No theological axioms or classical host axioms are imported as premises.
note: Issue #248 analytical vocabulary, scoped to this test. A source endorsement would require a separate passage-specific claim; the existing I.3.3 claim supplies only the narrow reading.
